iut_type: End Product (Toytec Bluetooth module), RF PHY test scope and cost tiers by supported PHY mode
customer_question: For RF PHY testing, we believe 1M-only testing is sufficient -- is 2M also required? And if 1M-only is acceptable, is the test cost lower?
question_variants: What does each additional RF PHY test tier (1M, 1M+2M, 1M+2M+Coded) actually cost?
What is the cost difference between testing 1M+Coded versus the full 1M+2M+Coded set?
actual_issue: The customer needed to confirm whether limiting RF PHY testing to 1M mode only (since their registered product only supports 1M) was sufficient, and whether doing so would reduce the test cost compared to testing additional PHY modes.
plain_english_explanation: RF PHY test scope is determined by which PHY modes the product being registered actually supports -- if the product only supports 1M mode, testing only 1M mode is sufficient and acceptable; there's no requirement to test modes the product doesn't implement. Cost scales with PHY mode scope: 1M-only testing (10 items) was quoted at ¥400,000, while progressively broader scope tiers added cost: 1M+2M (20 items) at ¥700,000, 1M+2M+Coded (28 items) at ¥900,000, and the full set including Stable Modulation Index items (51 items) at ¥1,500,000. An intermediate combination not in the original tier list, 1M+Coded without 2M (18 items), was also quoted at ¥700,000 when the customer later asked about it, noting this specific combination (Coded support without 2M support) is unusual and hadn't come up in the lab's prior experience.
consultant_answer: If your product only supports 1M mode, testing only 1M mode is sufficient -- there's no need to test modes it doesn't implement. Cost scales with scope: 1M-only (10 items) is ¥400,000; adding 2M (20 items total) is ¥700,000; adding Coded as well (28 items total) is ¥900,000; and including Stable Modulation Index items (51 items total) is ¥1,500,000. If you specifically want 1M+Coded without 2M (18 items), that's also ¥700,000, though this is an unusual combination we haven't seen requested before.
decision_logic: RF PHY test scope should match the PHY modes the registered product actually supports -- testing unsupported modes is unnecessary, and cost scales directly with the number of test items required by the chosen scope tier.
final_recommendation: When scoping RF PHY testing, confirm exactly which PHY modes the product supports before quoting, and present the cost tiers transparently (incremental scope vs. incremental cost) so the customer can choose the minimum sufficient scope for their actual product capability.
risk_if_done_wrong: Testing PHY modes the product doesn't actually support would waste cost on unnecessary test items, while testing too narrow a scope relative to the product's actual capabilities could leave required conformance evidence missing.
